object_description: ensemble of solitaires with the new wing set over-corner on the dominant slope edge
design_condition: the new wing occupies the dominant slope edge in an over-corner position, set back from the street, so that its volume with the gymnasium below connects the two levels of the school grounds

positive: The new volume with gymnasium below connects the two levels of the school grounds
Together with the workroom wing in front of it, the school square is spatially defined
The transparent ground floor with freely accessible circulation mediates between school square and landscape as a continuation of the slope edge
The spacious public uses support the view into the landscape
The school square becomes the central meeting point, providing identity and orientation
The volumetric disposition respectfully strengthens the site and the listed buildings as an ensemble
The slope edge is continued all the way to the street, creating an exciting sequence of streetscapes
Precise positioning lets the embankment edge develop a presence on the upper level and integrates the wooded area into the open space
The arrangement of the kindergarten outdoor space between the existing wing and the forest fragment is interesting
The workrooms above the fire station and the gymnasium can be optimally used outside school hours thanks to separate access
The generous foyer works as an extension of the square and cleverly mediates and separates
Rooms used outside school hours can be separated from the other school rooms for operational ease
Clusters dock over the corner to the centrally located covered atrium
The facade grid alluding to the 1950s ties in with the architectural language of the existing wing, and its colour accentuation mediates between the buildings
The steel frame with wooden box girder elements reduces the loads on the hall ceiling beams
The setting of the gymnasium limits excavation volume and pit securing costs
Structure, foundations and excavation support are clearly described
The compactness promises efficient use of financial resources and potential to meet sustainability goals
The proposed volumetry of two to three storeys blends in well with the existing ensemble despite its compact volume
A clear and convincing urban design with skilful handling of the topography
negative: It is questionable whether the respectful ensemble effect would survive the planned extension
Whether the rectangular parking along the street could be built this way needs clarification
The entrances to the ensemble are less convincing, with one street access not upgraded and others too informal
The circulation of children between main and multi-purpose rooms crosses the access to the upper floors and appears awkward
Room areas end up sometimes too small and sometimes too large
The childcare outdoor areas adjoin the parking and are not directly accessible from the childcare rooms
The layout creates a sports hall unevenly lit from northwest to northeast
The chosen hall access separates the direct connection between equipment room and hall
The group rooms are not located between the classroom units as required
The planned flexibility of the studios is called into question by the placement and necessity of the checkrooms
There is a lack of clear statements on the materialisation and structural design of the facades
The fire protection painting of the steel girders is costly for operation and maintenance
Whether the planned photovoltaic areas suffice would have to be proven
The limit has been reached in terms of protecting the surroundings of the listed wing
The distribution of uses shows deficits in some spatial arrangements and their operational dependencies
